summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV/AIDS, and ongoing MRSA bacteremia presented with palpitations and severe Clostridium difficile colitis. She had recently been treated with metronidazole but continued to have frequent diarrhea, leading to dehydration and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Intravenous fluids and oral vancomycin led to resolution of the arrhythmia and improvement in bowel symptoms. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.2, and warfarin was continued without bridging. She received hemodialysis during the admission and was discharged to an extended care facility to complete IV vancomycin for MRSA and a prolonged course of oral vancomycin for C. difficile, with close follow-up for anticoagulation and HIV management.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Nephritis and nephropathy, not specified as acute or chronic, with unspecified pathological lesion in kidney
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
